title: Company-wide policies and process documentation
author: Aisha Patel
body:
Overview:
This document consolidates Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and internal templates. It is intended as the single reference for employees and managers to understand responsibilities, approval workflows, and operational safeguards.

Scope and applicability:
- Applies to all full-time, part-time, and contractor personnel and to third-party vendors acting on behalf of Redwood.
- Operational guidance covers cloud and on-prem resources, procurement activities, and employee travel that use company funds.

1) Access and permissions (IAM / RBAC):
- Principle: Least privilege by default; role-based access with time-bounded elevations.
- Role definitions:
  - Owner: Full administrative access for a single system or service; typically one or two per service.
  - Admin: Configure and manage resources; no access to production secrets by default.
  - Developer/Engineer: Access to dev/test and limited staging resources.
  - Viewer: Read-only access for audits and reporting.
- Access request process (summary):
  1. Requestor submits an access request via the IT portal (link: /confluence/eng-infra/ci-cd-and-build/it-portal).
  2. Manager approval required for role grants beyond Viewer.
  3. Service owner or team lead must approve Owner/Admin roles.
  4. Access is granted with a TTL (default 30 days) for temporary elevations.
- Quarterly review: Team leads receiveIAM access review reminders; deprovisioning actions logged.
- MFA and device controls: MFA enabled for all privileged roles; corporate devices must be enrolled in MDM.

2) Change management (systems and infra):
- Principle: Minimize blast radius; enforce review and post-deploy verification.
- Change categories: Routine (pre-approved runbook), Standard (scheduled with peer review), Major (requires RFC and change window).
- Workflow:
  1. Create a change RFC in the Change Tracker (template available under Internal Templates).
  2. Identify owner, rollback plan, and SLO impact.
  3. Peer review + SRE sign-off for infra-facing changes.
  4. Schedule in the approved change window; notify impacted teams.
  5. Post-deploy verification checklist and 24-72h monitoring depending on risk.
- Emergency changes: Must be documented retroactively; perform an incident review if outage occurs.

3) Data management and classification:
- Data classes: Public, Internal, Confidential, Regulated (PHI/PII).
- Handling rules:
  - Public: No restrictions.
  - Internal: Store in company storage; encryption at rest recommended.
  - Confidential: Access limited to named roles; encryption at rest and in transit enforced; audit logging required.
  - Regulated: Must follow additional controls (KMS, customer-specific residency, restricted exports).
- Data retention: Default retention is 2 years for log telemetry and 7 years for financial records unless otherwise required by contracts or law.
- Data movement & transfers:
  1. Any transfer of Regulated data outside designated regions requires a Data Transfer Authorization (submit to security@redwood.ai).
  2. Use approved secure transport (SCP/SFTP/TLS) only.
- Backups and restore: Backup schedules are defined per service in system-specific runbooks; test restores quarterly.

4) Procurement and expenses:
- Procurement thresholds and approval matrix:
  - < $1,000: Team lead approval.
  - $1,000–$25,000: Department head approval (Finance notified).
  - > $25,000: Finance + Head of Procurement + Legal review as needed.
- Capital vs expense classification: Finance classifies based on contract length and asset type; contact finance@redwood.ai for ambiguitites.
- Purchasing process (summary):
  1. Use the company procurement portal and create a purchase request with vendor, cost center, and justification.
  2. Attach quotes/contract and preferred payment method.
  3. Obtain required approvals per approval matrix.
  4. Procurement team places the order and creates PO; vendor onboarding checklist executed for new vendors.
- Expense reporting: Employees submit expense reports within 30 days via ExpenseTool; receipts required for all transactions > $25.

5) Vendor management and onboarding:
- Vendor risk levels: Low, Medium, High (based on data access, criticality, and financial exposure).
- Onboarding checklist (minimum items):
  - Signed contract and scope of work.
  - Security questionnaire and completed SOC 2/ISO evidence where applicable.
  - Points of contact and escalation path.
  - Insurance certificates and IP clauses verified by Legal.
- Annual vendor review: Owners must perform an annual risk review for vendors classified Medium/High.
- Offboarding: Revoke access, collect company assets, confirm data disposition per contract.

6) Travel and business expense policy:
- Booking: Employees should use the approved travel portal; economy class for flights < 6 hours, business for approved long-haul or executive travel with Finance pre-approval.
- Per diem and lodging: Use company standard per-diem rates; exceptions require manager + Finance approval.
- Insurance and safety: Company travel insurance covers business trips; register international travel with People Ops.
- Expense submission: Submit within 14 days of travel completion with itemized receipts. Non-compliant claims may be denied.

7) Internal templates and operational artifacts:
- Available templates (links in portal):
  - Access Request Form (time-limited role grant)
  - Change Request (RFC) template
  - Vendor Onboarding Checklist
  - Travel expense template and pre-approval form
  - Data Transfer Authorization form
- How to use: Copy templates from the Templates library, fill required fields, and attach in the relevant tracker (Change Tracker, Procurement Portal, or Vendor Tracker).

8) Roles & ownership quick reference:
- People Ops: Travel policy, employee expense reimbursements, global benefits alignment.
- Finance: Expense approvals, PO issuance, capital classification, vendor payments.
- Legal: Contract review, IP, data residency clauses.
- InfoSec/Security: Data classification, authorization for Regulated data transfers, vendor security reviews.
- Service Owners/Engineering Leads: Approve access, own runbooks, sign off on changes impacting services.

9) Audit, metrics, and review cadence:
- Quarterly audits: Access reviews, vendor compliance checks for Medium/High vendors, procurement exceptions report.
- KPIs to track: number of temporary elevated accesses, change rollback rate, vendor overdue refreshes, expense report SLA (median days to reimbursement).
- Records retention: Policy artifacts and approvals retained per legal requirements; Financial records retained minimum 7 years.

Appendix A — Example Change Request checklist:
- RFC ID, owner, impact summary
- Rollback plan and validation steps
- Expected SLO impact (latency/errors/cost)
- Pre-deploy checklist items (backups, monitoring dashboards staged)
- Post-deploy validation and owner sign-off

Appendix B — Example access TTL policy (template):
- "requested_role": "Admin"
- "requestor": "user@example.com"
- "manager_approval": "yes"
- "ttl_days": "30"

Contact and escalation:
For questions or exceptions, contact People Ops (people-ops@redwood.ai) for travel and HR policy matters, Security (security@redwood.ai) for data/access exceptions, and Finance (finance@redwood.ai) for procurement questions.

- 2026-08-12: Clarified procurement thresholds and vendor review cadence.
- 2026-12-08: Updated access TTL default and added data transfer authorization procedure.
